reasoning: The accepted work was itself the redefinition: the person asked that an extra act beside an expected one count as a failure rather than a note. The procedure's shown-result clause states that a row's definition of done never names the person's eye as the check for an ordinary buildable result, and it names exactly this shape as the exception to the third reserved case — 'a redefinition he ordered himself is not that third case: he settled the fork when he ordered it, and carrying out his decision is executing it, not making it.' The four runs flipping from green to red is not a defect or an unplanned trade-off; it is the direct observable outcome of the admitted done — which recorded runs count as passing is precisely what the instruction moved, so 26-of-35 is the change working, not evidence against it. Nothing here is irreversible outside git, no numeric threshold was invented after start, and no artifact-unsettled product choice is open, so rule 12/27 reserve nothing for him. The pipeline's obligations are the ordinary ones: a verifier who is not the row's holder is handed the frozen DOD and the paths touched and re-grades the 35 recorded runs directly rather than trusting the producer's unit tests (the presence of a passing test is not the acceptance verdict), the confirmed-class sweep runs if the grader has sibling leniencies of the same kind, then verify, close the checkpoint in the same step, and report — naming plainly in the report that the score moved 30 → 26 and which four runs flipped, so he can disagree while undoing is cheap. If he then disagrees with the shown result, that is a new fact and a new row, not a reopening of this one.
